purpose: Teach: サタン/羽生/オスカー/クレア/フォックス/魔物/プリーズ/乞食

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんがオペラ「ファウスト」のサタンの場面に感動された
lines.en: When your father was young, Gran, he was deeply moved by the Satan scene in the opera Faust.
lines.style: Gentle, reflective opening. Slow, measured pace. The voice of someone reaching back into memory without urgency. Soft landing on the final word, as if placing the memory carefully.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: うん、お祖父ちゃん、若い頃、羽生善治名人の将棋を観られたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: Yes, and didn't your grandfather see Yoshiharu Habu play shogi when he was young, dear?
lines.style: Warm, playful counter-offer. Light curiosity in the voice — she's not correcting, she's offering her own memory back. Slight tease underneath. The rising inflection of gentle turn-taking.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんがアカデミー賞のオスカーの中継を観られた
lines.en: When your father was young, Gran, he watched the live broadcast of the Academy Awards and the Oscar ceremony.
lines.style: Same reflective quality as before. Unhurried. The memory lands with quiet significance — a shared cultural moment from decades past. Pause before 'ceremony' as if visualising it.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、若い頃、女優のクレア・ブルームを愛されたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: And didn't your grandfather love the actress Claire Bloom when he was young, dear?
lines.style: Warm, knowing smile in the voice. She's matched his memory-pace and raised him with her own. The name 'Claire Bloom' lands with a touch of affection — she knows this story. Gentle teasing warmth.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんが20世紀フォックスの映画を毎週観られた
lines.en: When your father was young, Gran, he used to watch the Twentieth Century Fox films every single week.
lines.style: The same patient, reflective tone. Slight emphasis on 'every single week' — the regularity of it speaks to devotion. Voice settles into the rhythm of habitual memory, comfortable and unhurried.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、若い頃、ホラー小説で魔物退治の物語を愛読されたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: Didn't your grandfather love reading horror novels about defeating monsters when he was young, dear?
lines.style: Affectionate, playful curiosity. The word 'monsters' carries a touch of lightness — she's enjoying this exchange. Warm familiarity underneath. The 'dear' at the end is a gentle anchor to their intimacy.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんが英会話で「プリーズ」を丁寧に使われた
lines.en: When your father was young, Gran, he spoke English very politely and always used 'please' with such care.
lines.style: Reflective, precise. The memory of his father's politeness colours the delivery — respect underneath. Slight warmth on 'please,' as if remembering the earnestness of youth. Settling, unhurried.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、若い頃、江戸時代の乞食、つまり物乞いの研究をされてたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: Didn't your grandfather spend his youth studying the history of beggars in the Edo period, dear?
lines.style: Warm, knowing smile. She's drawing him into the specificity of his own past — the unusual detail makes her tone more intimate, more playful. Closes gently with 'dear,' a soft landing that says 'I know all your stories.'
